page: Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton processors with Neoverse-V3 cores operating at 3.3 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor system, it features 48 dedicated physical CPU cores without hyperthreading, supplying 48 virtual CPUs. Memory allocation stands at 96.0 GB total, delivering a compute-centric ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor architecture includes 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. It lacks dedicated GPU acceleration and local instance storage, while providing a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the c9g.12xlarge demonstrates strong execution performance across single-threaded and multi-threaded operations. Geekbench results place it in the top tier for single-core (2387.0), multi-core (28306.0), and software compilation tasks (91952.0). Data processing capabilities are further illustrated by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 623.71 GB/sec. PassMark tests report high memory ratings alongside static web serving throughput of 103.35 GB/sec. In key-value database operations, the instance handles 136.88 million Redis SET operations per second and achieves fast prompt processing on lightweight large language model workloads.

The 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU allocation profile offers resource density for computational jobs where dedicated core execution is prioritized over extensive memory capacity. This design yields strong cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks such as automated build pipelines, code compilation, high-throughput web proxies, and in-memory caching. A notable trade-off is the reliance on network-attached storage due to the absence of local NVMe drives.
description: Amazon Web Services c9g.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance driven by 48 dedicated physical cores on 64-bit ARMv9 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V3 processors running at 3.3 GHz. Operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance pairs 48 vCPUs with 96.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It excludes local NVMe storage and discrete GPUs, relying on a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier results in single-core and multi-core Geekbench tests, software compilation, static web serving throughput reaching 103.35 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations exceeding 136 million ops/sec. Memory performance is supported by 48 MB of L3 cache and a high PassMark memory score. The server offers clear cost efficiency for parallel CPU workloads without requiring extensive memory overhead, making it well suited for continuous integration, code compilation, high-throughput web serving, and database cache operations.
